headline: Saudi Roads Authority Opens 40 Projects and 900km of Network in the First Half
deck: The half-year figures put the road programme's emphasis on freight corridors and regional links rather than new capacity around the largest cities.
excerpt: Saudi Arabia's Roads General Authority has reported 40 road projects opened in the first half of 2026, adding more than 900 kilometres to the national network across five regions. The authority also recorded 3.7 million truck journeys on the kingdom's logistics corridors over the same period.
content:
Saudi Arabia's Roads General Authority has opened 40 road projects in the first half of 2026, adding more than 900 kilometres to the national network, according to figures carried by the Saudi Press Agency.

The projects are spread across five regions — Makkah, Madinah, Asir, the Eastern Province and Qassim — rather than concentrated on the Riyadh and Jeddah conurbations where most road spending has gone in recent years. The authority framed the work around inter-city connection, journey times, and support for tourism and freight movement.

The more telling number in the half-year account is traffic rather than construction. The authority recorded more than 3.7 million truck journeys on the kingdom's logistics corridors during the six months, and issued more than 32,000 permits for services along the national road network. Those are operating figures, and they describe a road system being measured on what moves across it rather than on kilometres delivered.

That distinction matters for contractors. Road programmes in the kingdom have historically been counted in length and value at award. An authority reporting truck movements and service permits alongside project openings is describing a network it intends to manage as an asset, which points toward maintenance, operations and roadside services as a growing share of the work rather than greenfield alignment.

The regional spread is consistent with that reading. Asir and Qassim are not where the largest construction budgets sit, but they are on the corridors that connect the Red Sea coast and the central plateau to the Eastern Province industrial belt. Madinah's inclusion follows a broader pattern of investment in the routes serving religious tourism, where the constraint has been surface access rather than terminal capacity.

The half-year figures land against a road programme that has been running at a different scale in the capital. Riyadh has separately launched a road development package worth SAR 9.8bn, a figure that dwarfs any single item in the authority's regional list and reflects how far capital-region spending sits above the national baseline.

The Eastern Province has also moved in the same period. The province inaugurated six road projects worth SAR 406m and oversaw the signing of transport agreements exceeding SAR 3bn, according to the Saudi Gazette. Those agreements span roads, ports, airports and railways rather than roads alone, which is how the province has framed its transport position — as a logistics function rather than a construction programme.

For the supply chain behind these projects, the composition of the work is as relevant as its value. Forty projects averaging just over 22 kilometres each is a profile of many medium contracts rather than a few large ones, which favours contractors with regional depots and asphalt capacity over those geared to single large alignments. It is a different market from the one that built the kingdom's expressway spine.

The authority has not published a second-half target alongside the half-year figures, and the pace of openings in the first six months of a year is not a reliable guide to the full twelve in a programme where completions cluster around weather windows and budget cycles.
author: BrentDesk Staff
seoTitle: Saudi Roads Authority Opens 40 Projects, 900km in H1 2026
seoDescription: Saudi Arabia's Roads General Authority opened 40 road projects adding over 900km in the first half of 2026, and logged 3.7 million truck journeys.
replacementOf: Transport Ministry awards 41 road contracts, SAR 3bn
replacementReason: The MEED report of 41 road contracts worth SR3bn dates from 9 May 2012, not August 2026; the search summary misattributed it. Replaced with the Roads General Authority's H1 2026 half-year figures, which are corroborated across SPA/Arab News, TradeArabia and IndexBox.
